title: Ops incident scribe: runbook + customer update templates
content:
Purpose
This is a lightweight, practical runbook for drafting incident communications: internal war-room signals, customer-facing status page entries, email/portal update templates, and the minimum-safe checklist for early-stage comms. Use this as the on-call scribe's rapid-reference when an incident is declared.

Principles (tone & cadence)
- Be factual, concise, and repeatable.
- Communicate impact first (what, who, scope), then mitigation steps.
- Avoid speculation; label unknowns clearly (e.g., [investigating]).
- Maintain consistent cadence and update even when there is no progress. Silence is treated as no update.
- Differentiate internal detail vs customer-facing language (internal: technical; customer: impact + ETA + workaround).

Quick roles (first 10 minutes)
- Incident lead: coordinates updates and escalation (default: on-call for affected service).
- Scribe / Comms owner: writes the status page and customer messages.
- Tech lead / Investigator: leads triage and root-cause hypothesis.
- L2/L3 support: validates customer impact and surfaces high-priority customers.
- Escalation contact (exec): notified for Sev1 after 15 minutes if unresolved.

War-room checklist (minimum-safe checklist for scribe)
1) Create incident record (Jira/INC): title: [INC-{ID}] {Service} degraded/partial outage.
2) Set incident severity tag (Sev1/Sev2/Sev3) and add initial timeline.
3) Post first internal Slack message to #sre-ops with: short summary, link to incident, war-room link, required hands.
4) Publish initial status page entry (see "Status page wireframe") even if brief.
5) Notify Customer Success for affected accounts and collect VIP list.
6) Start 5-minute heartbeat cadence for updates in war-room channel.
7) Capture all commands and outputs in incident log; annotate any sensitive material.

Status page wireframe (short-form components)
- Header: Incident {INC-{ID}} — {Service Name} experiencing {degradation/outage}
- Impact: "Users may experience {errors/latency/failed requests} when {action}." Keep one sentence.
- Scope: "% of requests affected" or list of regions/paths. If unknown: "investigating scope".
- Start time: ISO timestamp (UTC).
- Current status: investigating / identifying root cause / mitigating / resolved.
- Next update: in {X} minutes (provide cadence).
- Links: incident tracker, public status page, customer support contact.
- Actions customers can take: show a short workaround if available.

Initial status page template (first-public update)
Title: "Service disruption: {Service} — {short impact summary}"
Body:
We are investigating an issue affecting {Service} that began at {Start time UTC}. Some customers may see {errors/failed requests/slower responses}. Our engineers are actively investigating.
What we know:
- Impacted: {percentage}/region/list of endpoints (if known)
- Customer-facing effect: {e.g., API 500s for batch endpoints} 
What we’re doing:
- Engineering is investigating and rolling back recent deploys where applicable.
- We’ve opened an internal incident and will post updates here every {X} minutes.
How this affects you:
- If you rely on {feature}, you may experience {symptom}. We’re prioritizing high-volume customers.
Workaround: {short bullet or "none at this time"}
Next update: {ETA or cadence}
Contact: {support@redwood.ai} or your CS rep for account-specific concerns.

Customer email template (short, for affected VIPs)
Subject: "{Service} impacting {customer_org} — {INC-{ID}}"
Hi {Customer Name},
We wanted to let you know we are investigating an issue impacting {Service} that may affect your usage. Our incident ID is {INC-{ID}}. We are prioritizing your account and will follow up with an update by {time UTC}.
Impact: {one-line precise impact}
Workaround / Mitigation: {if any}
If you need immediate help contact {cs_rep_name} or reply to this message.
Regards,
{SRE on-call name} / Redwood Inference Support

In-product banner / console banner text (short)
Banner line 1: "{Service} degraded — seeing errors/latency (INC-{ID})"
Banner line 2: "We're investigating and will update at {ETA}. See status.redwood.ai for details."

Internal Slack scripts (templates)
- Initial post to #sre-ops: "INC-{ID} | {Service} | Start {UTC} | Symptoms: {short} | War-room: {link} | Scribe: @{name} | TL: @{name} | Please join if available."
- 1st public-ready update: "INC-{ID} — publishing initial status page. Impact: {short}. Next update in {X}m."
- When mitigation in place: "INC-{ID} — mitigation deployed (what we rolled back or toggled). Verifying. ETA for full recovery {X}m."

Severity-specific guidance (short)
- Sev1 (full outage / customer-facing data loss risk): publish public update within 10 minutes, notify execs after 15m, email VIPs, post frequent updates every 10–15m.
- Sev2 (degraded service with partial impact): publish within 20 minutes, update every 20–30m.
- Sev3 (minor/no user impact): document internally, optional public note at end of incident.

When to escalate to legal/compliance/PR
- Any incident with customer data exposure, regulatory impact, or media interest -> notify Legal and PR immediately (via pager + email).
- Use the chain: SRE lead -> Director SRE -> Legal Counsel -> PR lead.

Post-incident comms (first 24–48h)
- Short follow-up public message: confirm resolution, quick summary of cause if known, and whether customer data was impacted (no details beyond factual statements).
- Targeted email to affected customers: recap of impact, timeline, mitigation, and who to contact for follow-up.
- Internal blameless timeline: gather notes in incident Jira within 24h and assign postmortem owner within 48h.

Common fillable placeholders (use these consistently)
- {INC-{ID}} — internal incident identifier
- {Service} — product surface (e.g., hosted-api, embeddings, console)
- {Start time UTC} — ISO format
- {ETA} — next update time or estimated recovery time
- {safety_note} — e.g., "No customer data exposure suspected at this time" or "Investigating potential data exposure"

Escalation matrix (contact snippets)
- On-call SRE: pager / Slack @oncall-sre (primary)
- Support escalation: cs-urgent@redwood.ai
- Exec notify (for Sev1 after 15m): ops-exec@redwood.ai

Examples (short, not exhaustive)
- Example 1 (Sev1 initial post):
Title: "API outage — generation requests returning 500s (INC-2026)"
Body: "We are investigating increased 500s for text generation beginning at 2026-03-12T17:02:00Z. Impact: majority of requests to /v1/generate may fail. Engineering is rolling back the deploy from 17:00 and will update in 10 minutes. No customer data exposure suspected. Contact support@redwood.ai for account-specific questions."

- Example 2 (Sev2 escalation update):
"INC-2027 — root-cause hypothesis: degraded KV cache leading to elevated latencies for long-context models. Mitigation: disabled cache priming for rollout group A. Observing partial recovery; next update in 20m."

Checklist for scribe handover (closing or handing to postmortem owner)
- Ensure status page shows final "resolved" and includes resolution summary.
- Send post-incident email to affected customers within 24h with summary + who to contact.
- Upload war-room logs to incident Jira and tag postmortem owner.
- Add timeline entries and label any follow-up actions (owner + due date).

Open questions / decisions to bake into a future canonical runbook
- Exact cadence for Sev2 vs Sev1 updates by product line (should latency-sensitive products get faster cadence?).
- Template for social media updates (shorter, approved wording) and PR notification thresholds.
- Whether to include syntactic change: auto-include "no data exposure" unless investigating (some teams prefer never to assert absence).

Notes & references
- See linked artifacts for incident tracking and postmortem template.
- Keep this doc intentionally short; expand with team-specific addenda as needed.

Scribe sign-off
Drafted by: Aisha Park (SRE)
Reviewers: Daniel Rivera, Mei Chen, Omar Haddad
Status: draft — feedback welcome in the #sre-runbooks channel.
